cards.explanation: The answer is horses. Isaiah says they "…rely on horses…" and then he keeps going with "…their abundance of chariots…" and "…their multitude of horsemen." (Isaiah 31:1). That's a whole stable and a parking lot of chariots, friends. Everything they're leaning on has hooves or wheels, and none of it is the LORD.

The answer is False, and Isaiah says it plainly: "They do not look to the Holy One of Israel; they do not seek the LORD." (Isaiah 31:1). Their eyes are on the horses, the chariots and the horsemen. The LORD isn't even on the list, friends, and that's exactly why the woe comes.

The answer is that He does not call them back. Isaiah says of the LORD, "He does not call back His words." (Isaiah 31:2). Once He's spoken, it stands. No take-backs. I wish I had that kind of follow-through, friends. I once said "just one more cookie" about forty times.

The answer is the allies of evildoers. Isaiah says He "…will rise up against the house of the wicked and against the allies of evildoers." (Isaiah 31:2). Notice that the helpers are in there too, not only the folks being helped. Think about that next time you're about to sign on with a crowd, friends.

The answer is that both of them perish. Isaiah says "…the helper will stumble, and the one he helps will fall; both will perish together." (Isaiah 31:3). The helper doesn't get to watch from the sidelines, and neither does the one leaning on him. It's like two people holding each other up on a wobbly ladder when the ground goes, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says the lion "…is not terrified by their shouting or subdued by their clamor…" (Isaiah 31:4). A whole band of shepherds is yelling, and that lion just keeps standing over its prey. I'd have been halfway to the next county, friends. My mustache would've been a white flag.

The answer is that He comes down to do battle. The LORD says, "…so the LORD of Hosts will come down to do battle on Mount Zion and its heights." (Isaiah 31:4). He's the one coming down, friends, and the lion picture is how He says it. Nobody's shouting Him off the mountain.

The answer is protect. "Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem." (Isaiah 31:5). Birds hover over what they're watching over, and that's the picture here. The verse goes on: "He will shield it and deliver it; He will pass over it and preserve it." Good, warm words after all that woe, friends.

The answer is that the message calls them to return to Him. It says, "Return to the One against whom you have so blatantly rebelled, O children of Israel." (Isaiah 31:6). The way back is open, friends, and it's a way home. I know a little about being found, so I like this one a lot.

The answer is idols. The message says, "…every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold that your own hands have sinfully made." (Isaiah 31:7). Their own hands made them, and the verse calls that sinful. I stamp cookies, friends, but I have never once asked a cookie for advice.

The answer is a sword not made by mortals. The LORD says, "a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals." (Isaiah 31:8). Assyria falls "…not by the sword of man…" No blacksmith signed that blade, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor." (Isaiah 31:8). Nobody stands and fights, friends. That's the opposite of standing their ground.

The answer is the sight of the battle standard. The LORD declares, "…their princes will panic at the sight of the battle standard…" (Isaiah 31:9). The sight of the standard is what sets them off, friends. I'd panic too if the oven timer went off and I hadn't started the dough.
